text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday there could be a deliberate attempt by some outsiders to undermine the peso.

"The unusual behaviour of the exchange rate as well as the obvious attacks on the peso .... indicate that there could be a deliberate effort to undermine the peso from outside sources," Ramos told his weekly news conference.
"We are also seeing a media disinformation campaign of some kind," he said.
Philippine ministers have twice denied articles by a Singapore newspaper this week over their reported comments about a possible devaluation of the Philippine currency.
The newspaper articles triggered attacks on the peso forcing the Central Bank to intervene heavily in the currency market and boost interest rates.

Ramos, who was replying to a question on how long the Central Bank would defend the peso, quoted the Central Bank as saying the country's economic fundamentals were strong and the situation did not warrant a change in the present market-determined exchange rate policy.
He said the Central Bank considered calls for a devaluation as meaningless as the exchange rate continues to realistically represent the market rate.
Pointing to volatility in the local stock market, he said this was not due to money leaving the country but moving to high-yielding local fixed income assets.
